answer: Validators lock 32 ETH collateral and face a quadratic slashing curve where each equivocation multiplies the penalty by the square of their stake share; a zero-knowledge verifiable delay forces any Sybil cluster of size n to incur O(n^2) capital, making marginal attack cost super-linear and exceeding any extractable value. Hence the expected attack utility is negative, yielding a robust Nash equilibrium where rational agents prefer honest validation over a coordinated fraud echo that would demand a sable shale of capital.
